topics.h: Ring, ring! Who is coming down the lane? It is a happy child on a bicycle!
p: The lesson 'My Bicycle' is a poem about the joy of riding a bicycle.
A poem has short lines. Many lines end with sounds that match.
Read slowly. Think about who, what, where and when.
The answer is often right there in a line of the poem.

ex.q:
Read this poem.
My bicycle is red and bright,
I ride it in the morning light.
Ring, ring! goes my little bell,
I wave to Ravi, he waves as well.
Up the lane and round the tree,
My bicycle is fun for me!
When does the child ride the bicycle?
st: Look for a line about time.
Line 2 says: 'I ride it in the morning light.'
So the child rides in the morning.

topics.rl: When you read a story book or a sign on the road, you look for who, what and where, just like this.

topics.h: Cat, hat, mat, bat! Why do these words sound like a song?
p: Rhyming words end with the same sound.
bright and light rhyme. bell and well rhyme.
Only the first sound changes: c-at, h-at, m-at.
Poems often use rhyming words at the end of lines.

ex.q: Which word rhymes with 'ride': slide or ring?
st: Say the end sound of ride: -ide.
slide ends with -ide too.
ring ends with -ing. That is different.

topics.rl: Many songs and nursery rhymes you sing in school use rhyming words.

topics.h: A bicycle has many parts. Can you name them all?
p: A bicycle has two wheels. 'Bi' means two.
We push the pedals with our feet. We turn the handlebar to steer.
We press the brakes to stop. We ring the bell to warn people.
Wear a helmet. Ride where an adult says it is safe.

ex.q: Meena sees a dog on the path ahead. Which part should she use to stop?
st: The bell only makes a sound.
The pedals make the bicycle go.
The brakes make the bicycle stop.

topics.rl: When you ride in your colony park, you ring the bell and use the brakes to keep everyone safe.

topics.h: A picture can tell a whole story without a single word. Let's read one!
p: The lesson 'Picture Reading' asks us to look at a picture and talk about it.
Ask: Who is there? What are they doing? Where are they?
Look for colours, numbers and small details.
Then say it in short sentences.

ex.q:
Imagine this park picture.
In the park, Arjun flies a yellow kite.
Two girls swing high on the swings.
A brown dog runs after a ball.
Dadi sits on a bench and smiles.
Who is sitting on the bench?
st: Find the line about the bench.
It says: 'Dadi sits on a bench and smiles.'
So Dadi is on the bench.

topics.rl: When you tell Mummy about your school trip, you are describing a scene.

topics.h: Run! Jump! Clap! Can you do these right now?
p: An action word tells what someone or something does.
run, jump, eat, sing, write and swim are action words.
Action words are also called doing words.
In 'Riya kicks the ball', the action word is 'kicks'.

ex.q: Find the action word: 'The baby claps.'
st: Ask: What does the baby do?
The baby claps.
So 'claps' is the action word.

topics.rl: In PT class, your teacher calls out action words: run, stop, jump, bend!

topics.h: Words are like beads. Put them in the right order to make a sentence necklace!
p: A sentence tells a full idea.
A sentence begins with a capital letter.
A telling sentence ends with a full stop (.).
Words must be in the right order to make sense.

ex.q: Put the words in order: dog / The / fast. / runs
st: Start with the word that has a capital letter: The.
Who? dog. What does it do? runs. How? fast.
The full stop comes at the end.

topics.rl: When you write in your notebook, your teacher checks for capital letters and full stops.

topics.t: A poem about play and nature
topics.h: Sun, trees, puddles and butterflies! What makes playing outside so much fun?
p: The lesson 'It is Fun' is a poem about the fun of play. Our own poem here is about playing outside in nature.
Nature means things not made by people: trees, sun, rain, birds and flowers.
Poems can use the same words again and again, like 'It is fun to...'.
Read each line and picture it in your mind.

ex.q:
Read this poem.
It is fun to run in the sun,
It is fun to rest under a tree,
It is fun to hop in the puddles,
And watch a butterfly, free.
Playing out with friends all day
Is the best fun for you and me!
What does the child hop in?
st: Find the line with 'hop'.
It says: 'It is fun to hop in the puddles.'
So the child hops in the puddles.

topics.rl: After the rain, children love to jump in puddles and watch butterflies in the garden.

topics.h: Look! The puppy is running, the baby is smiling and Dadi is singing!
p: Doing words tell what someone does: run, hop, sing, climb.
We can add -ing to show what is happening now: play → playing.
Some words change a little: run → running, dance → dancing.
We say 'is' for one and 'are' for many: 'The girl is playing.' 'The boys are playing.'

ex.q: Choose the right word: 'Look! The baby is ___.' (smiling / smile)
st: After 'is' we use the -ing word to show what is happening now.
'The baby is smiling.' sounds right.

topics.rl: When you tell your friend 'I am drawing' or 'We are playing', you use doing words.

topics.h: The swing goes up... and down! Up and down are opposites.
p: Opposite words mean very different things.
up – down, fast – slow, hot – cold, wet – dry.
big – small, day – night, happy – sad, open – close.
Opposites help us compare two things.

ex.q: Rohan runs fast. His little brother runs ___. Pick the opposite of 'fast'.
st: Fast means very quick.
The opposite of quick is not quick.
That word is 'slow'.

topics.rl: At the park, the slide takes you down and the steps take you up.

topics.h: Close your eyes. Can you still know what is around you? Yes, you can!
p: The lesson 'Seeing without Seeing' is about knowing the world without using our eyes.
We have five senses: sight, hearing, smell, taste and touch.
Eyes see. Ears hear. Nose smells. Tongue tastes. Skin feels.
When we cannot see, the other senses help us a lot.

ex.q: Your eyes are shut. You hear 'Moo!' Which sense helps you know a cow is near?
st: 'Moo' is a sound.
We hear sounds with our ears.
So hearing tells us a cow is near.

topics.rl: In the dark at night, you know Mummy is near when you hear her voice.

topics.t: Words for sounds, smells, tastes and touch
topics.h: Is it sweet or sour? Soft or rough? Let's find words for what we feel!
p: Taste words: sweet, sour, salty, bitter.
Touch words: soft, hard, rough, smooth, hot, cold.
Sound words: loud, soft, quiet.
These words help us describe things even with our eyes shut.

ex.q:
Read this.
Tara closes her eyes.
She hears a whistle. It is the pressure cooker!
She smells hot pakoras.
She touches her cat. It is soft.
She tastes a sweet laddoo. Yum!
Which sense tells Tara about the pakoras?
st: Find the line about pakoras.
It says: 'She smells hot pakoras.'
We smell with our nose.

topics.rl: When you eat a lemon or touch a smooth stone, you use these words to tell your friends.

topics.t: Being kind to people who cannot see
topics.h: Can you read a book with your fingers? Some people do it every day!
p: Some people cannot see. We say they are visually impaired.
Many of them read Braille. Braille has tiny raised dots that you feel with your fingers.
Louis Braille made this way of reading. He could not see either.
A white cane helps a person feel the path ahead.
To help, first ask kindly: 'May I help you?' Tell them your name when you talk.

ex.q:
Read this.
Aman cannot see.
He reads with his fingers.
His book has tiny raised dots.
He walks with a white cane.
He loves music and chess.
How does Aman read his book?
st: Find the line about reading.
It says: 'He reads with his fingers.'
The raised dots are Braille.

topics.rl: Many lift buttons have raised dots next to the numbers so people who cannot see can use them.

topics.t: A poem about a friend going away
topics.h: Your best friend is going away for the holidays. What will you say?
p: The lesson 'Come Back Soon' is a poem about going away on a trip and coming back soon. Our own poem here is about a friend going away.
When a friend goes away, we miss them.
We say goodbye and hope to meet again soon.
Look for feeling words in a poem. They tell us how someone feels.

ex.q:
Read this poem.
My friend Neha goes away today,
To her nani's house for a holiday.
I wave my hand and say goodbye,
A little tear comes to my eye.
'Come back soon, we'll play again!
We'll swing and sing in the summer rain!'
Where is Neha going?
st: Find the line about where Neha goes.
It says: 'To her nani's house for a holiday.'
So Neha is going to her nani's house.

topics.rl: In the summer holidays, many friends go to their grandparents' homes. We wave goodbye and wait for them.

topics.h: Smiles, tears, frowns and giggles! Our faces show how we feel.
p: Feeling words tell how we feel inside.
happy, sad, angry, scared, excited, proud, surprised.
When a friend goes away, we may feel sad. When they come back, we feel happy.
All feelings are okay. It helps to talk about them.

ex.q: Kiran wins the drawing prize at school. Which feeling word fits best?
st: Winning a prize is a good thing.
We feel good about what we did.
That feeling is called proud.

topics.rl: When you tell Papa 'I am scared of the thunder', he knows how to help you.

topics.h: Magic words open hearts! Do you know them?
p: We say 'Hello' or 'Good morning' when we meet someone.
We say 'Goodbye', 'Bye' or 'See you soon' when we leave.
'Please', 'Thank you' and 'Sorry' are kind words.
We say 'Good night' before we sleep.

ex.q: Ali's cousin is going back home on the train. What can Ali say?
st: The cousin is leaving.
We wish people well when they leave.
Ali can say: 'Goodbye! Have a safe trip!'

topics.rl: At the end of a school day, you wave and say 'Bye! See you tomorrow!' to your friends.

topics.t: Places on the way to school
topics.h: What do you see on your way to school every day? Let's take a walk!
p: The lesson 'Between Home and School' is about the places we pass on the way to school.
We may pass shops, a park, a bus stop, a post office or a big tree.
Words like first, next, then and after tell us the order.
Always cross the road at a zebra crossing, holding an adult's hand.

ex.q:
Read this.
Every day, Sonu walks to school with Papa.
First, they pass the milk booth.
Next, they cross the road at the zebra crossing.
Then they walk past a big banyan tree.
The school gate is just after the post office.
What do they pass first?
st: Look for the word 'First'.
It says: 'First, they pass the milk booth.'
So the milk booth comes first.

topics.rl: You can tell a new friend how to reach your school by naming the places on the way.

topics.h: Your friend is lost! Can you tell her the way?
p: Direction words tell us which way to go.
left and right are opposites. 'Turn left' or 'Turn right'.
'Go straight' means keep going ahead. Do not turn.
near means close by. far means a long way off.

ex.q: Directions: 'Walk straight. Turn left at the fruit shop. The library is on your right.' Where do you turn?
st: First you walk straight.
The direction says 'Turn left at the fruit shop'.
So you turn at the fruit shop.
ex.a: At the fruit shop, you turn left

topics.rl: When an auto driver asks 'Left or right?', you can tell him the way to your house.

topics.h: Where is my school bag? In, on or under the bed?
p: Position words tell us where something is.
in, on, under, behind, in front of, next to, between.
'The cat is under the table' means the cat is below the table.
'Sonu sits between Ravi and Meena' means Ravi is on one side and Meena on the other.

ex.q: The pencil is inside the box. Which position word fits? 'The pencil is ___ the box.'
st: Inside means it is in the box.
The word for inside is 'in'.

topics.rl: When Mummy asks 'Where are your shoes?', you say 'Under the bed!' That is a position word.

topics.h: Honk! Ring! Swish! A town is full of sounds and busy people!
p: The lesson 'This is My Town' is a poem about a town and the places in it.
A town has markets, parks, roads, shops and homes.
Many people work in a town to help us.
Rhyming words make the poem fun to read aloud.

ex.q:
Read this poem.
This is my town, so busy and bright,
The market is full from morning to night.
The bus says 'honk', the cycles ring,
In the park the children swing.
The postman brings a letter to me,
I love my town, as you can see!
What does the postman bring?
st: Find the line with 'postman'.
It says: 'The postman brings a letter to me.'
So he brings a letter.

topics.rl: Look around your own town or village. What places and helpers do you see?

topics.h: Need a book? A train? A doctor? Every place in a town has a job!
p: We buy fruits and vegetables at the market.
We go to the hospital when we are very ill.
We borrow books from the library. We keep money safe in a bank.
We catch a train at the railway station. We post letters at the post office.

ex.q: Arjun wants to read a story book but does not want to buy one. Where can he go?
st: He wants to read, not buy.
A library lends books for some days.
So he can go to the library.

topics.rl: Next time you go out with your family, name the places you pass.

topics.h: Who stitches your school uniform? Who mends your slippers? Our helpers do!
p: Community helpers do work that helps all of us.
A doctor and a nurse look after sick people.
A tailor stitches clothes. A cobbler mends shoes. A carpenter makes things from wood.
A farmer grows food. A firefighter puts out fires. A teacher helps us learn.
We should thank our helpers and treat them with respect.

ex.q: The strap of Riya's sandal is broken. Who can mend it?
st: A sandal is a kind of shoe.
A cobbler mends shoes and sandals.
So Riya should go to the cobbler.

topics.rl: Say 'Thank you' to the guard, the bus driver and the cleaner in your school. They help you every day.

topics.h: Look up! Is that cloud a rabbit, a ship or an elephant?
p: The lesson 'A Show of Clouds' is about the shapes we see in clouds.
Clouds are made of tiny drops of water.
The wind moves clouds and changes their shapes.
Dark grey clouds often bring rain.

ex.q:
Read this.
Pari lies on the grass and looks up.
One cloud looks like a fluffy rabbit.
One looks like a big elephant.
The wind blows. The rabbit turns into a boat!
Pari laughs. 'The sky is a magic show!'
What does the rabbit cloud turn into?
st: Find the line about the rabbit changing.
It says: 'The rabbit turns into a boat!'
So it becomes a boat.

topics.rl: On a holiday afternoon, lie on a mat on the terrace with an adult and look for cloud shapes.

topics.h: Shut your eyes and think of a pink elephant. Can you see it? That is imagination!
p: To imagine means to make a picture in your mind.
A cloud is not really an animal. We only imagine it is.
We can say a cloud 'looks like' a rabbit or 'is like' a ship.
Clues help us imagine: long ears could be a rabbit, a trunk could be an elephant.

ex.q: A cloud has a long neck and four thin legs. What animal could it look like?
st: Think of an animal with a very long neck.
A giraffe has a long neck and thin legs.
So the cloud could look like a giraffe.

topics.rl: When you play 'house-house' or pretend a stick is a horse, you are using your imagination.

topics.h: A cloud can be white, fluffy, big or dark. These words paint a picture!
p: Describing words tell us more about a person, animal, place or thing.
They can tell colour (white), size (big), shape (round) or feel (soft).
In 'The white cloud floats', the describing word is 'white'.
Describing words make our sentences more fun to read.

ex.q: Find the describing word: 'Ravi has a big umbrella.'
st: Ask: What kind of umbrella?
A big umbrella.
So 'big' is the describing word.

topics.rl: When you tell Mummy 'I want the red balloon, not the blue one', you use describing words.

topics.h: Your name is the very first gift you got! Do you know what it means?
p: The lesson 'My Name' is a story about a little fly who forgets his own name. Names matter!
Every person has a name. It tells others who we are.
Many names have a meaning. Kamal means lotus. Tara means star.
Some people have a pet name too, like Chintu or Pinky.
We should say everyone's name correctly and kindly.

ex.q:
Read this.
Hello! My name is Kamal.
My name means lotus.
My Dadi chose my name.
My friends call me Kamu.
I like my name very much!
Who chose Kamal's name?
st: Find the line with 'chose'.
It says: 'My Dadi chose my name.'
So Dadi chose it.

topics.rl: Ask your family who chose your name and what it means. It is a lovely story!

topics.h: Names are special, so they wear a crown: a capital letter!
p: Names of people begin with a capital letter: Riya, Kabir, Asha.
Names of places begin with a capital letter too: Delhi, Pune, India.
The word I is always a capital letter.
Other words like cat, tree and ball do not need a capital letter in the middle of a sentence.

ex.q: Fix the names: 'meena lives in jaipur.'
st: meena is a person's name → Meena.
jaipur is a place's name → Jaipur.
Meena is also the first word, so it needs a capital anyway.

topics.rl: Look at the name on your notebook cover. It starts with a capital letter!

topics.h: K-A-B-I-R! Can you spell your name like a spelling champion?
p: We spell a name by saying its letters one by one: R-A-V-I.
Count the letters to check your spelling. Ravi has 4 letters.
Names can be put in ABC order by their first letter.
Write your own name with care, with a capital letter first.

ex.q: Put these names in ABC order: Chetan, Anu, Bina.
st: Look at the first letters: C, A, B.
In the alphabet, A comes first, then B, then C.
So: Anu, Bina, Chetan.

topics.rl: Your class register lists names in ABC order. That is why Aarav is called before Zoya!

topics.h: Caw, caw! Who is that on the wall every morning?
p: The lesson 'The Crow' is about a bird we see almost every day.
A crow is mostly black. It has a strong beak.
It says 'caw, caw'. It eats grains, fruits, insects and leftover food.
Crows make nests of twigs in trees. They often live in groups.
Crows are very clever birds. By eating scraps, they help keep places clean.

ex.q:
Read this.
Kaalu the crow sits on the wall.
'Caw, caw!' he calls in the morning.
He is black and shiny, with a strong beak.
He eats grains, fruits and bits of roti.
He makes a nest of twigs in the neem tree.
Kaalu is a very clever bird!
Where does Kaalu sit?
st: Look at the first line.
It says: 'Kaalu the crow sits on the wall.'
So he sits on the wall.

topics.rl: Look out of your window in the morning. You may see crows on the wall or on a tree.

topics.h: Everything has a name: you, your dog, your school and your pencil!
p: A naming word is the name of a person, animal, place or thing.
Person: Ravi, teacher. Animal: crow, cow. Place: school, Delhi. Thing: pen, cup.
In 'The crow sits on the wall', crow and wall are naming words.
Naming words answer 'Who?' or 'What?'

ex.q: Find the naming words: 'Meena feeds the crow.'
st: Who feeds? Meena. That is a person.
Feeds what? The crow. That is an animal.
'feeds' is a doing word.

topics.rl: When you make a shopping list for Mummy, like milk, bread and eggs, you write naming words!

topics.h: One crow on the wall... then five crows! How do we say 'many'?
p: One means just one. Many means more than one.
Add -s to many words: crow → crows, nest → nests, tree → trees.
Add -es to words ending in s, x, ch or sh: bus → buses, box → boxes.
Use the 'many' word when there is more than one: 'three crows'.

ex.q: One box. Two ___.
st: box ends with x.
For words ending in x, we add -es.
box → boxes.

topics.rl: At the fruit shop you say 'one banana' but 'six bananas'.

topics.h: A monkey on a crocodile's back in the middle of a river! How will he escape?
p: In the lesson 'The Smart Monkey', a monkey is wiser than people think. Here we read another smart-monkey tale: an old Indian folk tale about a monkey and a crocodile.
A folk tale is a story told by grandparents to children for many, many years.
In this tale, a clever monkey uses his brain to stay safe.
Read the story in order: beginning, middle and end.

ex.q:
Read this story.
A monkey lived in a jamun tree by a river.
He gave sweet jamuns to his friend, the crocodile.
The crocodile said, 'Sit on my back. Come to my home.'
In the river, he said, 'My wife wants to eat a monkey's heart!'
The monkey stayed calm. 'I left my heart in the tree! Let's go back.'
At the tree, the monkey jumped up to a high branch. He was safe!
How did the monkey get back to the tree?
st: The monkey said his heart was in the tree.
The crocodile believed him and swam back.
So the monkey used a clever trick.
ex.a: He tricked the crocodile into taking him back.

topics.rl: Ask your Dadi or Nani to tell you a folk tale. Many of them have clever animals!

topics.h: When trouble comes, don't panic! Think like the smart monkey.
p: Presence of mind means staying calm and thinking quickly in trouble.
The monkey did not cry. He thought of a plan.
If you are in trouble, stop, take a deep breath and think.
Ask a trusted adult for help: a parent, a teacher or a police officer.

ex.q: Arya gets lost in a crowded mela. What should she do?
st: Stop and stay calm. Do not run about.
Find a police officer or a helper at the mela.
Tell them her name and her parent's phone number.
ex.a: Stay calm and ask a police officer or mela helper for help.

topics.rl: Learn your parent's phone number by heart. It helps if you are ever lost.

topics.h: Clever or foolish? High or low? Let's play with words from the story!
p: Clever means smart. The opposite of clever is foolish.
A river bank is the land at the side of a river.
The monkey jumped up to a high branch. The opposite of high is low.
The monkey was safe. The opposite of safe is in danger.

ex.q: The monkey was clever. The crocodile believed a silly trick. Which word fits the crocodile: clever or foolish?
st: The crocodile believed the monkey's heart was in the tree.
That was not smart.
So the crocodile was foolish.

topics.rl: When you play 'opposites' with your friends, you use pairs like high – low and sweet – sour.

topics.h: One drop is tiny. But many drops can fill a bucket! How?
p: The lesson 'Little Drops of Water' is a poem. It shows that small things add up to big things.
Many little drops make a bucket full of water.
Many small good deeds make the world a kinder place.
'Little by little' means slowly, a small bit at a time.

ex.q:
Read this poem.
One little drop goes plip, plop, plip,
Into my bucket, drip, drip, drip.
Drop after drop, it fills up high,
Enough for my plants when they are dry.
Little by little, small things grow
Into big things. Now you know!
What fills up the bucket?
st: The poem says 'Drop after drop, it fills up high'.
So many small drops fill the bucket.

topics.rl: Putting one coin in your piggy bank every day adds up to a lot of coins!

topics.h: Every drop counts! Can you be a Water Hero today?
p: All living things need water. Clean water is precious.
Most water on Earth is salty sea water. We cannot drink it.
Turn off the tap while brushing your teeth.
Tell an adult about a leaking tap so it can be fixed.
Use the water from washing vegetables to water the plants.

ex.q: Kabir leaves the tap running while he brushes his teeth. What should he do?
st: Running water goes down the drain and is wasted.
He needs water only to wet the brush and rinse.
So he should turn off the tap while brushing.
ex.a: Turn off the tap while brushing.

topics.rl: Some homes and schools in India collect rainwater on the roof and store it to use later.

topics.h: Rain + bow = rainbow! Some words are made of two small words.
p: Two small words can join to make a new word: rain + coat = raincoat.
rain + bow = rainbow. water + fall = waterfall.
A puddle is a small pool of rainwater on the ground.
A river flows. A pond is still. The sea is big and salty.

ex.q: Neha wears something to stay dry in the rain. It is made of 'rain' + 'coat'. What is it?
st: Join the two words.
rain + coat = raincoat.

topics.rl: In the monsoon, you wear a raincoat, jump over puddles and maybe see a rainbow!

topics.h: Different languages, clothes and foods, but one big family! Who are we?
p: The lesson 'We Are All Indians' is about how people in India are different, yet one.
People in India speak many languages, wear many kinds of clothes and eat many foods.
We are different in many ways, but we live together as friends.
'Unity in diversity' means being one, even when we are different.

ex.q:
Read this.
In our class there are children from many states.
Anjali speaks Tamil. Gurpreet speaks Punjabi.
Joy speaks Bengali. Meera speaks Marathi.
We eat different foods and wear different clothes.
But we all study, play and laugh together.
We are all Indians!
Which language does Meera speak?
st: Find Meera's name in the passage.
It says: 'Meera speaks Marathi.'
So Meera speaks Marathi.

topics.rl: Your class may have friends who speak different languages at home. You all learn and play together!

topics.h: Vanakkam! Namaskar! Sat Sri Akal! Hello in many languages!
p: India has many states. Many states have their own main language.
Tamil Nadu – Tamil. Kerala – Malayalam. Karnataka – Kannada.
West Bengal – Bengali. Gujarat – Gujarati. Punjab – Punjabi. Maharashtra – Marathi.
Hindi is spoken in many states, like Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Rajasthan.
Many people in India speak two or more languages.

ex.q: Riya is going to visit her cousin in Gujarat. Which language will she hear the most there?
st: Find the state: Gujarat.
The main language of Gujarat is Gujarati.
The names sound alike: Gujarat → Gujarati.

topics.rl: Look at an Indian currency note. The amount is written in many Indian languages!

topics.t: Symbols and festivals that join us
topics.h: One flag, one anthem, and festivals all year round! What do we share?
p: Our national flag has three colours: saffron on top, white in the middle and green at the bottom.
A navy blue wheel called the Ashoka Chakra is in the middle. It has 24 spokes.
Our national anthem is 'Jana Gana Mana'. National bird: peacock. National animal: tiger.
We celebrate Independence Day on 15 August and Republic Day on 26 January.
Harvest festivals: Pongal in Tamil Nadu, Onam in Kerala, Bihu in Assam, Baisakhi in Punjab.

ex.q: Our flag has three colours in bands. Which colour is at the bottom?
st: The top band is saffron.
The middle band is white, with a navy blue wheel.
The bottom band is green.

topics.rl: On 15 August and 26 January, schools hoist the flag and sing 'Jana Gana Mana' together.

qa.q: Poem line: 'My bicycle is red and bright.' What colour is the bicycle?
qa.e: The line says the bicycle is red and bright.

qa.q: Poem line: 'Ring, ring! goes my little bell.' What goes ring, ring?
qa.e: The line says 'my little bell' goes ring, ring.

qa.q: Poem line: 'I wave to Ravi, he waves as well.' What does Ravi do?
qa.e: 'He waves as well' means Ravi also waves.

qa.q: Poem line: 'Up the lane and round the tree.' What does the child ride round?
qa.e: The line says the child rides round the tree.

qa.q: Poem line: 'My bicycle is fun for me!' How does the child feel?
qa.e: Fun things make us happy. The child enjoys the bicycle.

qa.q: What is the lesson 'My Bicycle' mainly about?
qa.e: The poem talks about the joy of riding a bicycle.

qa.q: Which word rhymes with 'bike'?
qa.e: bike and like both end with the -ike sound.

qa.q: Which word rhymes with 'wheel'?
qa.e: wheel and seal both end with the -eel sound.

qa.q: Which word rhymes with 'ring'?
qa.e: ring and sing both end with the -ing sound.

qa.q: Which pair of words rhymes?
qa.e: cat and mat both end with -at. The other pairs only start the same.

qa.q: Which word does NOT rhyme with 'tree'?
qa.e: tray ends with an -ay sound. tree, bee, see and knee end with -ee.

qa.q: Rhyming words have the same ___ at the end.
qa.e: Rhyming is about sound. bell and well sound the same at the end.

qa.q: How many wheels does a bicycle have?
qa.e: A bicycle has two wheels. 'Bi' means two.

qa.q: Which spelling is correct?
qa.e: We spell it b-i-c-y-c-l-e.

qa.q: Which thing keeps your head safe when you ride?
qa.e: A helmet is hard and strong. It protects your head if you fall.

qa.q: Which part do you push with your feet to make the bicycle go?
qa.e: Your feet push the pedals round and the wheels move.

qa.q: Kabir wants to turn left on his bicycle. What does he turn?
qa.e: We turn the handlebar to steer the bicycle left or right.

qa.q: Which is a safe thing to do on a bicycle?
qa.a: Ring the bell to warn people
qa.e: Ringing the bell tells people you are coming. The others can cause a fall.

qa.q: Scene: 'Arjun flies a yellow kite.' What colour is the kite?
qa.e: The scene says the kite is yellow.

qa.q: Scene: 'Two girls swing high on the swings.' How many girls are on the swings?
qa.e: The word 'two' tells us there are 2 girls.

qa.q: Scene: 'A brown dog runs after a ball.' What does the dog run after?
qa.e: The scene says the dog runs after a ball.

qa.q: In 'Arjun flies a kite in the park', which words tell WHERE?
qa.e: 'In the park' tells us the place. That answers 'where?'

qa.q: Which sentence describes a market scene?
qa.e: In a market, people buy and sell things like fruits and vegetables.

qa.q: Which question helps you find WHO is in a picture?
qa.e: 'Who' asks about people or animals in the picture.

qa.q: Which one is an action word?
qa.e: We can jump. It is something we do.

qa.q: Find the action word: 'Riya kicks the ball.'
qa.e: 'Kicks' tells what Riya does.

qa.q: Which action word fits? 'Birds ___ in the sky.'
qa.e: Birds fly in the sky.

qa.q: Find the action word: 'Dadi cooks dal.'
qa.e: 'Cooks' tells what Dadi does.

qa.q: Which word is NOT an action word?
qa.e: A cup is a thing. We cannot 'cup'. sing, dance and read are actions.

qa.q: Action words are also called ___ words.
qa.e: Action words tell what we do, so they are called doing words.

qa.q: Which sentence is written correctly?
qa.e: It begins with a capital letter and ends with a full stop.

qa.q: Which word order makes a sentence?
qa.e: 'The cat drinks milk.' makes sense. The others are mixed up.

qa.q: What comes at the end of a telling sentence?
qa.e: A telling sentence ends with a full stop (.).

qa.q: Which word should begin with a capital letter? 'my dog is brown.'
qa.e: 'my' is the first word of the sentence, so it needs a capital M.

qa.q: Picture: a boy is drinking water. Which sentence matches?
qa.e: It says the right person (boy) and the right action (drinks water).

qa.q: Which one is a full sentence?
qa.e: It tells a full idea: who (Sita) and what she does (plays with a top).

qa.q: Poem line: 'It is fun to rest under a tree.' Where does the child rest?
qa.e: The line says the child rests under a tree.

qa.q: Poem line: 'And watch a butterfly, free.' What does the child watch?
qa.e: The line says the child watches a butterfly.

qa.q: Poem line: 'It is fun to run in the sun.' Which word rhymes with 'run'?
qa.e: run and fun both end with the -un sound. (sun rhymes too!)

qa.q: Which of these is a part of nature?
qa.e: A tree grows on its own. Phones, cars and TVs are made by people.

qa.q: Poem line: 'Playing out with friends all day.' Who does the child play with?
qa.e: The line says 'with friends'.

qa.q: Our poem says 'It is fun to run in the sun' and 'hop in the puddles'. What is our poem mainly about?
qa.e: The poem talks about playing outside with trees, sun and butterflies.

qa.q: Find the doing word: 'The children play in the park.'
qa.e: 'Play' tells what the children do.

qa.q: Which -ing word is spelt correctly?
qa.e: run becomes running. We write one more n before -ing.

qa.q: Which doing word goes best with 'a kite'?
qa.e: We fly a kite. We do not eat, drink or sleep a kite!

qa.q: Which word is a doing word?
qa.e: We can climb. Tree and sun are things. Happy is a feeling.

qa.q: Choose the right word: 'The ducks ___ swimming in the pond.'
qa.e: Ducks means many, so we use 'are'.

qa.q: What is the -ing word for 'dance'?
qa.e: We drop the e and add -ing: dancing.

qa.q: What is the opposite of 'open'?
qa.e: We open a box and then close it. They are opposites.

qa.q: What is the opposite of 'fast'?
qa.e: Fast means quick. Slow means not quick.

qa.q: What is the opposite of 'wet'?
qa.e: Wet clothes have water. Dry clothes have no water.

qa.q: The sun shines in the day. The moon shines at ___.
qa.e: Day and night are opposites. We see the moon at night.

qa.q: Which pair of words are opposites?
qa.e: Big and small mean very different things. The other pairs mean almost the same.

qa.q: The see-saw goes up and ___.
qa.e: One end goes up and the other end goes down.

qa.q: We hear with our ___.
qa.e: Ears catch sounds. That is how we hear.

qa.q: Which part of the body helps you taste food?
qa.e: The tongue tells us if food is sweet, sour or salty.

qa.q: How many senses do we have?
qa.e: Sight, hearing, smell, taste and touch. That is five.

qa.q: Which sense tells you that a rose smells nice?
qa.e: We smell with our nose.

qa.q: You touch a cat's fur with your eyes shut. Which sense are you using?
qa.e: We feel things with our skin. That is the sense of touch.

qa.q: The pressure cooker whistles. Which sense tells you this?
qa.e: A whistle is a sound. We hear it with our ears.

qa.q: Passage: 'She hears a whistle. It is the pressure cooker!' What makes the whistle?
qa.e: The passage says the whistle is the pressure cooker.

qa.q: Passage: 'She touches her cat. It is soft.' How does the cat feel?
qa.e: The passage says the cat is soft.

qa.q: Passage: 'She tastes a sweet laddoo.' How does the laddoo taste?
qa.e: The passage says it is a sweet laddoo.

qa.q: Which word tells how a lemon tastes?
qa.e: A lemon makes your mouth pucker. It tastes sour.

qa.q: How does the bark of an old tree feel?
qa.e: Tree bark has bumps and cracks. It feels rough.

qa.q: Which one is a sound word?
qa.e: Loud tells us about a sound, like a drum or thunder.

qa.q: Passage: 'His book has tiny raised dots.' What are these dots called?
qa.e: Raised dots that people read with their fingers are called Braille.

qa.q: Passage: 'He walks with a white cane.' How does the cane help Aman?
qa.e: The cane touches the ground ahead and finds steps and bumps.

qa.q: Passage: 'He loves music and chess.' What does Aman love?
qa.e: The passage says he loves music and chess.

qa.q: Who made the Braille way of reading?
qa.e: Braille is named after Louis Braille, who made it.

qa.q: You see a person with a white cane at a step. What should you do first?
qa.e: Asking first is polite. They can tell you how to help.

qa.q: You meet a friend who cannot see. What is a kind thing to do?
qa.a: Tell your name when you speak
qa.e: They cannot see your face, so telling your name helps them know you.

qa.q: Poem line: 'A little tear comes to my eye.' How does the child feel?
qa.e: Tears often come when we are sad. The child will miss Neha.

qa.q: Poem line: 'I wave my hand and say goodbye.' What does the child do?
qa.e: The line says the child waves a hand and says goodbye.

qa.q: Poem line: 'My friend Neha goes away today.' Who is Neha?
qa.e: The line says 'My friend Neha'.

qa.q: Poem line: 'Come back soon, we'll play again!' What does the child hope?
qa.a: Neha comes back and they play
qa.e: The child wants Neha to come back so they can play again.

qa.q: Which word rhymes with 'goodbye'?
qa.e: goodbye and eye both end with the same 'eye' sound.

qa.q: Poem line: 'To her nani's house for a holiday.' Who is Neha going to meet?
qa.e: Nani is Neha's grandmother. She is going to nani's house.

qa.q: Ravi gets a new puppy. How does he feel?
qa.e: A new puppy is a lovely thing. Ravi feels happy.

qa.q: Meera's best friend moves to another city. How does Meera feel?
qa.e: She will miss her friend, so she feels sad.

qa.q: There is a loud thunder at night. Chotu hides under his blanket. How does he feel?
qa.e: Hiding from a loud noise shows Chotu is scared.

qa.q: Tomorrow is the school picnic! Anu can't wait. How does she feel?
qa.e: 'Can't wait' means she is very excited.

qa.q: Someone takes your pencil without asking. You may feel ___.
qa.e: Taking things without asking is not nice. It can make us upset.

qa.q: Kiran opens a box and finds a gift she did not expect! How does she feel?
qa.e: When something happens that we did not expect, we feel surprised.

qa.q: You meet your teacher at school in the morning. What do you say?
qa.e: We greet people with 'Good morning' in the morning.

qa.q: Before you sleep, what do you say to your family?
qa.e: We say 'Good night' before going to sleep.

qa.q: Your friend gives you a birthday card. What do you say?
qa.e: We say 'Thank you' when someone gives us something.

qa.q: You step on your friend's foot by mistake. What do you say?
qa.e: We say 'Sorry' when we hurt someone by mistake.

qa.q: Which words mean almost the same as 'Goodbye'?
qa.e: 'See you later' is said when we leave, just like 'Goodbye'.

qa.q: Your friend is leaving for a trip. What is a kind thing to say?
qa.e: Wishing a nice trip shows you care about your friend.

qa.q: Passage: 'Next, they cross the road at the zebra crossing.' Where do they cross the road?
qa.e: The passage says they cross at the zebra crossing.

qa.q: Passage: 'Then they walk past a big banyan tree.' Which tree do they pass?
qa.e: The passage says 'a big banyan tree'.

qa.q: Passage: 'The school gate is just after the post office.' What comes just before the school gate?
qa.e: 'Just after the post office' means they pass the post office and then reach the gate.

qa.q: Passage: 'Every day, Sonu walks to school with Papa.' Who walks with Sonu?
qa.e: The passage says Sonu walks with Papa.

qa.q: Where is the safest place to cross a road?
qa.e: Drivers know to stop at a zebra crossing. Cross there with an adult.

qa.q: Which word tells what happens first?
qa.e: 'First' tells us what comes before everything else.

qa.q: What is the opposite of 'left'?
qa.e: Left and right are the two sides. They are opposites.

qa.q: 'Go straight' means you should ___.
qa.e: Straight means ahead, with no turning.

qa.q: Directions: 'Walk straight. Turn left at the fruit shop. The library is on your right.' Where is the library?
qa.e: The directions say 'The library is on your right'.

qa.q: Your school is 5 minutes away. Nani's village is 5 hours away. Which is far?
qa.e: 5 hours is a long time to travel, so Nani's village is far.

qa.q: Which one is a direction word?
qa.e: 'Left' tells us which way to go.

qa.q: Directions: 'At the bus stop, turn right.' What should you do at the bus stop?
qa.e: The directions say to turn right at the bus stop.

qa.q: The cup is on top of the table. 'The cup is ___ the table.'
qa.e: On top of means 'on'.

qa.q: The cat hides below the bed. 'The cat is ___ the bed.'
qa.e: Below means 'under'.

qa.q: Sonu sits between Ravi and Meena. Who sits next to Sonu?
qa.e: Between means one is on each side. So both Ravi and Meena are next to Sonu.

qa.q: The tree is at the back of the house. 'The tree is ___ the house.'
qa.e: At the back of means 'behind'.

qa.q: Which one is a position word?
qa.e: 'Under' tells us where something is.

qa.q: The milk booth is beside the bus stop. 'The milk booth is ___ the bus stop.'
qa.e: Beside means 'next to'.

qa.q: Poem line: 'The market is full from morning to night.' When is the market full?
qa.e: The line says the market is full from morning to night.

qa.q: Poem line: 'In the park the children swing.' Where do the children swing?
qa.e: The line says the children swing in the park.

qa.q: Poem line: 'The bus says honk, the cycles ring.' What says 'honk'?
qa.e: The line says 'The bus says honk'.

qa.q: Poem line: 'I love my town, as you can see!' How does the child feel about the town?
qa.e: The child says 'I love my town'.

qa.q: Which word rhymes with 'bright'?
qa.e: bright and night both end with the -ight sound.

qa.q: Poem line: 'In the park the children swing.' Which word rhymes with 'swing'?
qa.e: swing and ring both end with the -ing sound.

qa.q: Where do we go to borrow books?
qa.e: A library lends books. We return them after reading.

qa.q: Where can Papa keep money safe?
qa.e: A bank keeps people's money safe.

qa.q: Where are fire engines kept?
qa.e: Fire engines and firefighters wait at the fire station.

qa.q: Where do we catch a train?
qa.e: Trains stop at the railway station.

qa.q: Mummy needs tomatoes and onions. Where will she go?
qa.e: We buy vegetables at the market.

qa.q: Dadu has a very high fever. Where should he go?
qa.e: Doctors and nurses look after sick people at the hospital.

qa.q: Who stitches clothes?
qa.e: A tailor uses a sewing machine to stitch clothes.

qa.q: Who makes tables and chairs from wood?
qa.e: A carpenter works with wood.

qa.q: Who grows rice and wheat?
qa.e: Farmers grow crops like rice and wheat in fields.

qa.q: Who puts out fires?
qa.e: Firefighters come in a fire engine and put out fires.

qa.q: A little boy is lost in the market. Who can help him find his family?
qa.e: Police officers help people who are lost and keep us safe.

qa.q: Who looks after sick people in a hospital with the doctor?
qa.e: Nurses care for sick people and help the doctor.

qa.q: Story: 'One cloud looks like a fluffy rabbit.' What does this cloud look like?
qa.e: The story says the cloud looks like a fluffy rabbit.

qa.q: Story: 'The wind blows. The rabbit turns into a boat!' Why does the cloud change shape?
qa.e: The wind blows the cloud and changes its shape.

qa.q: Story: 'Pari lies on the grass and looks up.' Where is Pari?
qa.e: The story says Pari lies on the grass.

qa.q: Pari says, 'The sky is a magic show!' What does she mean?
qa.a: The clouds keep changing like magic
qa.e: The cloud shapes keep changing, so it feels like a magic show.

qa.q: Clouds are made of tiny drops of ___.
qa.e: Clouds are made of very small water drops.

qa.q: Dark grey clouds fill the sky. What will Amma most likely carry?
qa.e: Dark grey clouds often bring rain, so an umbrella is useful.

qa.q: A cloud has a long curly trunk. What could it look like?
qa.e: An elephant has a long trunk.

qa.q: A cloud has two long ears on top. What could it look like?
qa.e: A rabbit has two long ears.

qa.q: What does 'imagine' mean?
qa.a: To make a picture in your mind
qa.e: When we imagine, we make a picture in our mind.

qa.q: Which sentence is imagined, not real?
qa.a: A cloud lion roars at the sun.
qa.e: Clouds cannot roar. It is a make-believe idea.

qa.q: A cloud is long and thin like a rope. What could it look like?
qa.e: A snake is long and thin.

qa.q: Which phrase do we use to say what a cloud seems to be?
qa.e: We say 'The cloud looks like a ship.'

qa.q: Find the describing word: 'The white cloud floats.'
qa.e: 'White' tells us what the cloud is like.

qa.q: Which one is a describing word?
qa.e: 'Tall' tells us what something is like.

qa.q: Pick the best word: 'Before the rain, the clouds are ___.'
qa.e: Rain clouds are dark grey.

qa.q: Find the describing word: 'The huge elephant drinks water.'
qa.e: 'Huge' tells us how big the elephant is.

qa.q: Describing words tell us what a person or thing is ___.
qa.e: Describing words tell what something is like: big, soft, red.

qa.q: Which describing word tells about colour?
qa.e: Blue is a colour. Soft is feel, big is size, round is shape.

qa.q: Passage: 'Hello! My name is Kamal.' What is the child's name?
qa.e: The child says, 'My name is Kamal.'

qa.q: Passage: 'My name means lotus.' What does the name Kamal mean?
qa.e: The passage says Kamal means lotus.

qa.q: Passage: 'My friends call me Kamu.' What is 'Kamu'?
qa.e: Kamu is a short, loving name his friends use. It is a pet name.

qa.q: A new friend says your name the wrong way. What is a kind thing to do?
qa.a: Tell them gently how to say it
qa.e: Gently showing them helps them learn your name.

qa.q: Why do we have names?
qa.a: So others know who we are
qa.e: Names help people know and call each one of us.

qa.q: The name Tara means ___.
qa.e: Tara means star.

qa.q: Which name is written correctly?
qa.e: A person's name begins with a capital letter. Only Riya does.

qa.q: Which word needs a capital letter? 'I play with sonu.'
qa.e: Sonu is a person's name, so it needs a capital S.

qa.q: Which place name is written correctly?
qa.e: Place names begin with a capital letter. Mumbai has a capital M.

qa.q: Why does 'Ravi' begin with a capital R?
qa.e: Names of people always begin with a capital letter.

qa.q: In which sentence are all the capital letters right?
qa.e: Asha and Pune are names, and both have capital letters. The sentence starts with a capital too.

qa.q: The word 'I' is always written as ___.
qa.e: 'I' is always a capital letter, even in the middle of a sentence.

qa.q: How many letters are in the name 'Meena'?
qa.e: M-e-e-n-a. That is 5 letters.

qa.q: Which name begins with the letter S?
qa.e: Sonu begins with S.

qa.q: Which name comes first in ABC order?
qa.e: Anil begins with A. A comes first in the alphabet.

qa.q: Ravi spells his name aloud. Which is right?
qa.e: Ravi is spelt R-A-V-I.

qa.q: What is the last letter of the name 'Kabir'?
qa.e: K-a-b-i-r. The last letter is r.

qa.q: How many letters are in the name 'Zoya'?
qa.e: Z-o-y-a. That is 4 letters.

qa.q: Passage: "'Caw, caw!' he calls in the morning." What sound does the crow make?
qa.e: The passage says Kaalu calls 'Caw, caw!'

qa.q: Passage: 'He makes a nest of twigs in the neem tree.' What is the nest made of?
qa.e: The passage says the nest is made of twigs.

qa.q: Passage: 'He eats grains, fruits and bits of roti.' Which food is NOT in this line?
qa.e: The line names grains, fruits and roti. Ice cream is not there.

qa.q: Passage: 'He makes a nest of twigs in the neem tree.' Where is Kaalu's nest?
qa.e: The passage says the nest is in the neem tree.

qa.q: Passage: 'Kaalu is a very clever bird!' Which word tells us Kaalu is smart?
qa.e: 'Clever' means smart.

qa.q: Passage: 'He is black and shiny, with a strong beak.' What colour is Kaalu?
qa.e: The passage says he is black and shiny.

qa.q: Which one is a naming word?
qa.e: 'Crow' is the name of an animal.

qa.q: Find the naming word: 'The crow sits on the wall.'
qa.e: 'Crow' names an animal. (Wall is a naming word too.)

qa.q: Which naming word is the name of a place?
qa.e: A school is a place. Ravi is a person, crow an animal, pen a thing.

qa.q: Which naming word is the name of an animal?
qa.e: A tiger is an animal.

qa.q: How many naming words are in 'The cat drinks milk.'?
qa.e: cat and milk are naming words. 'drinks' is a doing word.

qa.q: Naming words are names of people, animals, places and ___.
qa.e: Naming words name people, animals, places and things.

qa.q: One crow, many ___.
qa.e: We add -s to crow to make crows.

qa.q: One box, many ___.
qa.e: Box ends with x, so we add -es: boxes.

qa.q: One bus, two ___.
qa.e: Bus ends with s, so we add -es: buses.

qa.q: Which is the right word? 'I see three ___ on the wall.'
qa.e: Three means more than one, so we say crows.

qa.q: Which word is for just ONE thing?
qa.e: 'Tree' is one. trees, birds and cups mean many.

qa.q: One dish, many ___.
qa.e: Dish ends with sh, so we add -es: dishes.

qa.q: Story: 'A monkey lived in a jamun tree by a river.' Where did the monkey live?
qa.e: The story says he lived in a jamun tree by a river.

qa.q: Story: 'He gave sweet jamuns to his friend, the crocodile.' What did the monkey give?
qa.e: The story says the monkey gave sweet jamuns.

qa.q: Story: 'Sit on my back. Come to my home.' How did the monkey go into the river?
qa.e: The crocodile asked the monkey to sit on his back.

qa.q: The monkey said, 'I left my heart in the tree!' Why did he say this?
qa.a: It was a trick to get back safely
qa.e: Nobody can leave their heart behind. It was a clever trick.

qa.q: Story: 'At the tree, the monkey jumped up to a high branch.' How did the story end?
qa.e: The story ends with: 'He was safe!'

qa.q: At the start of the story, the monkey and the crocodile were ___.
qa.e: The monkey gave jamuns to 'his friend, the crocodile'.

qa.q: What does 'presence of mind' mean?
qa.e: It means you keep calm and think fast when there is trouble.

qa.q: How did the monkey show presence of mind?
qa.a: He stayed calm and thought of a trick
qa.e: He kept calm and quickly made up a clever plan.

qa.q: You are lost in a big market. What is a smart thing to do?
qa.a: Stay calm and ask a police officer
qa.e: A police officer can help you find your family safely.

qa.q: Your friend falls and hurts her knee in the park. What should you do first?
qa.a: Stay calm and call an adult
qa.e: An adult can help clean and treat the hurt knee.

qa.q: Which word means the same as 'calm'?
qa.e: Calm means quiet and peaceful, not upset.

qa.q: Which helps most when you are in trouble?
qa.e: A calm mind can think of a good plan, like the smart monkey did.

qa.q: The jamun tree is on the bank of the river. What is a river bank?
qa.a: Land at the side of a river
qa.e: The bank of a river is the land along its side.

qa.q: What is the opposite of 'clever'?
qa.e: Clever means smart. Foolish means not smart.

qa.q: What is the opposite of 'high'?
qa.e: A high branch is far up. Low means near the ground.

qa.q: What is the opposite of 'sweet'?
qa.e: Sweet like sugar, sour like a lemon.

qa.q: Which word means 'smart'?
qa.e: Clever and smart mean the same.

qa.q: Where does a crocodile live?
qa.a: In rivers and on their banks
qa.e: Crocodiles swim in rivers and lakes and rest on the banks.

qa.q: Poem line: 'Into my bucket, drip, drip, drip.' Where do the drops fall?
qa.e: The line says the drops fall into my bucket.

qa.q: Poem line: 'Drop after drop, it fills up high.' What happens to the bucket?
qa.e: Drop after drop, the bucket fills up high.

qa.q: Poem line: 'Enough for my plants when they are dry.' Who will get the water?
qa.e: The water is enough for the dry plants.

qa.q: 'Little by little, small things grow into big things.' What does this mean?
qa.a: Many small bits together make something big
qa.e: Small drops or small steps, added up, become big.

qa.q: Which word rhymes with 'high'?
qa.e: high and dry both end with the 'eye' sound.

qa.q: Ria puts 1 coin in her piggy bank every day for 10 days. How many coins does she have?
qa.e: 1 coin each day for 10 days makes 10 coins. Small things add up!

qa.q: What should you do while brushing your teeth?
qa.e: Turning off the tap saves the water that would go down the drain.

qa.q: A tap at school is leaking. What should you do?
qa.a: Tell a teacher so it can be fixed
qa.e: A leaking tap wastes water. A grown-up can get it fixed.

qa.q: Mummy washed the vegetables. What is the best use of that water?
qa.e: Plants can use the water. It is not wasted.

qa.q: Which usually uses less water for a bath?
qa.e: A bucket holds a fixed amount of water, so we use less.

qa.q: Most of the water on Earth is in the ___.
qa.e: Most of Earth's water is in seas and oceans. It is salty.

qa.q: Why should we save water?
qa.a: Clean water is precious and everyone needs it
qa.e: We all need clean water to live, and there is not a lot of it.

qa.q: rain + bow = ?
qa.e: Join rain and bow to get rainbow.

qa.q: Which place has salty water?
qa.e: Sea water is salty.

qa.q: What is a small pool of rainwater on the road called?
qa.e: A puddle is a small pool of rainwater on the ground.

qa.q: Water falling down from a high rock is called a ___.
qa.e: water + fall = waterfall.

qa.q: Which is a sound that water drops make?
qa.e: Water drops go drip, drip.

qa.q: Which word is made by joining two small words?
qa.e: rain + drop = raindrop.

qa.q: Passage: 'Anjali speaks Tamil.' Which language does Anjali speak?
qa.e: The passage says Anjali speaks Tamil.

qa.q: Passage: 'Joy speaks Bengali.' Who speaks Bengali?
qa.e: The passage says Joy speaks Bengali.

qa.q: Passage: 'But we all study, play and laugh together.' What do the children do together?
qa.e: The passage says they study, play and laugh together.

qa.q: What does 'unity in diversity' mean?
qa.a: Being one, even when we are different
qa.e: Unity means being one. Diversity means being different. We are one, even when we are different.

qa.q: Passage: 'We are all Indians!' What is the same about all these children?
qa.e: Their languages, foods and clothes are different, but they are all Indians.

qa.q: Your new classmate speaks a different language at home. What is a kind thing to do?
qa.a: Ask them to teach you a word
qa.e: Learning a word from a friend shows respect and makes you closer.

qa.q: The main language of Kerala is ___.
qa.e: People in Kerala mostly speak Malayalam.

qa.q: Kannada is the main language of which state?
qa.e: Kannada is the main language of Karnataka.

qa.q: Hindi is spoken in many states. Which of these is one of them?
qa.e: Hindi is the main language of Uttar Pradesh.

qa.q: Odia is the main language of which state?
qa.e: Odia is the main language of Odisha.

qa.q: People in Punjab mostly speak ___.
qa.e: Punjabi is the main language of Punjab.

qa.q: Marathi is the main language of which state?
qa.e: Marathi is the main language of Maharashtra.

qa.q: Which colour is at the top of our national flag?
qa.e: The top band of the flag is saffron.

qa.q: What colour is the Ashoka Chakra in the middle of the flag?
qa.e: The Ashoka Chakra is a navy blue wheel.

qa.q: How many spokes does the Ashoka Chakra have?
qa.e: The Ashoka Chakra has 24 spokes.

qa.q: What is the national bird of India?
qa.e: The peacock is our national bird.

qa.q: When do we celebrate Independence Day?
qa.e: India became free on 15 August 1947. We celebrate it every year.

qa.q: Onam is a harvest festival of which state?
qa.e: Onam is the harvest festival of Kerala.
